frequency_question: What proportion of major expiring transboundary water treaties successfully secure a signed successor agreement before or immediately upon expiration?
membership_rule: Includes formal treaties governing shared river basins between adjacent sovereign states that had defined expiration or renegotiation clauses. Excludes unilateral declarations, non-binding memorandums without resource-allocation frameworks, and internal state water compacts.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named major international basin renewals; population is small because permanent transboundary treaties of this scale are rare.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller bilateral sub-basin agreements in Europe and Africa that operate under different institutional density.
skeleton: Four major foundational transboundary river basin frameworks globally that faced operational renewal or structural successor milestones, compared against the specific friction of bilateral hydropolitics.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 major historical comparative episodes of foundational basin renewals.
validity_reason: International water law norms and hydro-diplomatic frameworks change slowly over multi-decade horizons.
